fieldValues.title: RFC-043 pointers: must a write that points anchorInstanceId or identityInstanceId at a non-member be refused?
fieldValues.thinking_reached: Checked 2026-11-09 with release build.639. container update {anchorInstanceId: <non-member>}, container create with a non-member anchor, and container update <root> {identityInstanceId: <non-member>} each return ok, and repo validate then reports container-pointer-unresolved errors. Removing the member a pointer names is refused ([R7], arrangement-pointer). RFC-043 [R3] says the pointer MUST equal a member, but [R7] mandates whole rejection only for [R2] violations and pointer-target removal, so write-time refusal of a pointer move is not ruled. No issue tracks it (#891, #907, #837 closed, other scope).
fieldValues.tensions: Option A: extend [R7] (an RFC-043 revision, Door 3) so any write that leaves a pointer unresolved is refused, the same as removal. Option B: keep [R3] as a validate-time rule only; a write may pass through an invalid state. Destructive and partial writes succeed silently (SP-06) and the affirmed remedy 'Every write refuses loudly what it cannot carry' pull toward A; editors that set the pointer before adding the member pull toward B.
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: 1. Does any client set the pointer before the member exists (srs-web, muDemocracy site editor)? 2. Should create and update be treated alike? Evidence that would choose: a search of client code for anchorInstanceId writes.
fieldValues.next_action: Owner: choose A or B. Recommendation: A, after the client search shows no pointer-first writes.
